column2: The central open question of the whole investigation, held open deliberately. Every piece of evidence on this site is ultimately argued against this page.
Ten inches of dirt reportedly taken out of the courtyard, and pavers laid over the ground where he fell. Whatever residue that soil held is gone.
600,000 files handed over, with the raw data reportedly withheld. Volume becomes its own kind of concealment when the useful part is the part that is missing.
A witness says the FBI asked him to delete his own footage. It is one of the sharpest cover-up claims on the site — and it is a claim, attributed to the witness who made it.
Standard forensic tests that were reportedly never run. In a case where residue and trace evidence would decide the argument, what was skipped shapes the record as much as what was found.
Explosive-detection dogs were reportedly stood down before the event. If a device belongs on the table at all, that decision is where to start.
Four proposed federal laws modelled on the Epstein Files Act. Sealed warrants, intelligence files and a mandated investigation — the mechanism for forcing out what is still not public.
Engraved bullets, wrapped in a towel, left on a roof. It is the detail the government's story struggles hardest to carry, and the page works through why.
A .30-06 carries roughly 2,900 foot-pounds, about eight times a 9mm. Commentators argue the wound described publicly does not match that much energy, and nobody has closed the gap.
The single largest independent engine driving this investigation into public view. Several of the document trails cited across this site surfaced first on her episodes.
The Bridgehampton gathering of early August 2025, and what people present say was asked of Charlie Kirk. Attendance is documented; pressure is alleged.
The body camera on the officer who reached the roof reportedly died there. The minutes it would have covered are the exact minutes everyone is arguing about.
The spinal cord is the part of the body that would settle the trajectory argument, and it is the part missing from the account. When it was removed, and by whom, is still unanswered publicly.
The state's own brief describes a downward trajectory. The damage described runs C2 to C7. The page sets the two side by side and lets the geometry speak.
Professional four-channel audio recorded about forty-six meters from the tent. Researchers say it separates a distant blast from a much louder event at the stage — two sounds, two places.
The personal and ideological motive the state and the press assembled. Read it as the account to be tested, because testing it is what the rest of this site does.

Two names sit at the centre of everything: the man who was killed and the man the state charged. The page holds them side by side without deciding either question, and routes to the sections where each is argued out.

Family, spouse, partner, colleagues — the people whose names travel with the case for no reason except proximity. The page exists to explain why each name appears at all, and to say plainly that appearing is not evidence.

The full roster: every person profile on the site, grouped by how they entered the record — security, TPUSA staff, witnesses, donors, officials, citizen investigators. Start here when you have a name and no idea where it fits.

A Texas charity filing and two county property histories, surfaced by @1MrsWhistledown and reproduced here as primary records. Forming a charity and buying a house are lawful acts; the page prints the documents and leaves the timing question open.

The FBI field office lead changed a month before September 10. So did Utah's chief medical examiner. This page maps the officials and institutions whose ordinary roles put them inside the case, and points to where each decision is argued.
Everyone who was close enough to see it, carry him, film it, or later take the record apart. Grouped by role rather than by theory, because a witness list is not a suspect list.

One name out of the large attendee cohort standing in the courtyard. Its value is collective rather than individual: crowd density, acoustic character and post-shot movement get established by many small accounts, never by one.
A military whistleblower reportedly described a seven-hour interrogation at Fort Huachuca led by a "Captain Neff" — on September 9, the day before. No official source has confirmed any part of it.
A name that surfaced once inside the SU-BTT and Egyptian-jet speculation and never again. It is recorded here for one reason: to mark it unsupported rather than let it keep circulating unchallenged.

A serving Navy captain whose son the FBI briefly named and then released. The page carries the chain-of-coincidence argument that put him into commentary, and states plainly that an argument is not a finding.
Officer Bagley testified he could not remember the plain-clothes man standing beside him on the roof. An X user reportedly put a name to that face — an influencer identification, not an official one.

One of the men who reportedly helped carry Charlie Kirk from the stage, with blood visible on his clothing in the footage. Clothing that close to the wound is forensic material — if it was ever tested.

The only FBI witness reported to have taken the stand at the July 2026 preliminary hearing, and the defense called her. Her subject: mixture DNA on the towel around the rifle and on the rooftop screwdriver.

A private individual named in a charity filing and a December 2025 transfer into a family trust. Both are ordinary lawful steps; the page prints them only because the family name entered the record through someone else.
A defense attorney whose Substack became the public's document library for this case. When a page here cites a filing, this is very often where the filing itself actually lives.

A TPUSA photographer standing feet away when it happened. Commentary notes that he and Andrew Sypher reportedly used similar language about the blast coming from inside the shirt — shared briefing, or two people perceiving the same thing.

TPUSA's communications chief and the show's executive producer — the man who shaped what the organisation said in the hours afterwards. He sits at the third vertex of the McCoy–Neff–Kolvet post-shot cluster.

Chief Field Officer since 2016, listed among the staff in close proximity to the stage. The field-operations layer decides who stood where on the perimeter, which is exactly what the courtyard footage keeps failing to settle.
He argued the state's account against Candace Owens on a national stream and put Tyler Robinson's likelihood at 75–85 percent. She put it at zero. The gap is the public argument in one number.
A claimed medical-examiner appointment that no official record supports. The page exists to say so, because an unverified staffing rumour repeated often enough starts to read like a fact.

A retired police officer of about twenty years who was walking toward the doors when she heard it. She recognised the man arrested from earlier events — and said outright she did not know whether he was the shooter.

On the sound and AV crew roster, close to the stage. AV personnel are the only people who can speak to how the microphone was rigged, routed and recovered, which makes the roster matter more than it looks.
A Florida faith leader named in secondary reporting on the July 31, 2025 off-the-record White House session. Reported attendance is the whole of the claim, and nothing about it is a finding.

A former Goldman Sachs trader turned pro-Israel influencer, named among those reportedly at the Bridgehampton gathering of August 4–5, 2025 — the meeting Candace Owens later called the Hamptons intervention.
UVU's president on the day, who resigned in 2026. GRAMA records reportedly show her cabinet received a "plan" contact on September 9 — the night before.

One of the most prominent pro-Israel voices in American media, and a fixture in the donor and media commentary around Charlie Kirk's last months. He is named in that commentary only; no involvement is alleged.
A single unverified claim about one security staffer's résumé is the entire content of the connection. The page records the claim and says clearly that it establishes nothing at all.
Tennessee's governor appears here because commentators laid his ordinary trade trip and a diplomatic meeting alongside a reported threat timeline. That juxtaposition is theirs, not this site's.

A retired Air Force brigadier general who reportedly said on Newsmax that "something exploded on him," and rejected the spine-impact explanation. A military opinion, offered explicitly outside any courtroom.

His footage is among the most-examined video records of the moment itself. The forensic questions about that file — metadata, frames, what it does and does not show — keep resurfacing in coverage of the state's case.

"Gibby" in the footage threads: one of the men who reportedly carried Charlie Kirk out, with significant blood on his clothing. Of everyone in the courtyard that day, he had some of the most direct physical contact.

A producer who said publicly that he witnessed Mikey McCoy's calls — set against a 12:24:02 frame that appears to show McCoy alone. Either the frame or the memory is wrong, and both are on the record.

A senior defense official whose name entered the case only through other people's flight threads. This site makes no claim that he was aboard anything or anywhere; the page records what was said, and by whom.
A campus-adjacent videographer whose independent footage fills the gaps left by TPUSA production cameras and by the institutional cameras that were never released.
A named procedural role and nothing beyond it. The page records that role with attribution because the alternative — letting a name float unexplained through commentary — is worse.
A name inside circulating, uncorroborated speculation about search-engine activity among Timpanogos-area medical staff. The site does not repeat the speculation; it marks it unsupported.
The citizen investigator behind this site, publishing as HolonCitizen. His frame-by-frame Stairs Guy comparison is the open-source work the identity gap pages are built on.

A co-owner of Hardscape Specialties LLC, named in unverified commentary about post-event paving in the courtyard. The paving question itself is real and unresolved; his involvement in anything improper is not alleged.
The ZUMA photojournalist whose stills from the courtyard have been pulled apart frame by frame. Professional press coverage, examined here as evidence rather than as illustration.

The man this entire investigation is about: founder of TPUSA, shot at roughly 12:23 p.m. on September 10, 2025. Every other thread — motive, timeline, forensics, cover-up — runs back through this page.

TPUSA's head of security, and one of five people in the SUV that left the campus. The Signal thread carrying death threats reportedly reached him, which makes what was known beforehand a live question.
Utah's chief medical examiner, newly in the role. Her autopsy report reached the court through Agent David Hull rather than from her own mouth on the stand.

A name on the reported pre-September-10 TPUSA board roster. Board composition matters because what the organisation did next is one of the case's open questions — but sitting on a board is not a claim.

Charlie Kirk's widow, who took a public leadership role at TPUSA after September 2025 and attended the July 2026 hearing sessions. The page records public roles and court attendance, and nothing more.

He asked Charlie Kirk the last question Charlie Kirk ever answered. He is an event witness rather than a hearing witness — a distinction this site keeps insisting on, because the two carry different weight.
UVU's police chief commanded roughly six officers for an event with a rooftop nobody was on. The perimeter and rooftop failures begin with how thin that contingent was.

Tyler Robinson's partner and roommate, charged with nothing, pulled into the record by the state's own investigation. Her messages and her phone became evidence in a case where she is not a defendant.

The sheriff at the centre of the September 11 surrender. The unresolved detail is the clock: commentary contrasts a reported 8:02 p.m. account with a 6:25 p.m. custody time, and hours matter for everything that followed.
He took over the FBI's Salt Lake City field office in August 2025 and led the September 11 press conference. Citizen researchers keep returning to the timing: a new lead, one month before.

The state charged him; this site examines whether the released evidence supports it. Start with the weapon: the .30-06 account is the government's narrative, and the ATF report came back inconclusive.
An Egyptian-registered aircraft that flight-trackers pulled into the case. The page separates what the ADS-B record actually shows from what the threads made of it.
No publicly reported gunshot-residue result. For a case built on a rifle fired from a roof, the missing test speaks louder than any test that was performed.
The figure on the stairs and the man in custody, compared frame by frame on build, gait and clothing. The gap between them is the whole argument.
No counter-snipers, no Secret Service, an overlooked rooftop, and a speaker with a documented threat history. This page is about what was not there.
An off-the-record White House session on July 31, 2025 — with the pro-Israel organising world present and TPUSA reportedly not. Absence, in this case, is the data point.
12:23 or 12:27 — the two times circulate as if interchangeable. They are not: four minutes changes who was where, and every timeline on the site depends on which is right.

The finding citizen investigators on X have converged on: a device at the microphone, not a round from a roof. It is the single largest divergence between the public record and the government's account.
The Army's intelligence hub, and a Special Air Mission jet tracked through it on September 8–9, 2025. A whistleblower account of a long interrogation sits on top of that flight data.
The roof the government says the shot came from. Every part of it — line of sight, the lip, the drop, the screwdriver — has been measured by people who do not accept that account.
Two men reportedly contacted UVU the night before to discuss a "plan." What the university did with that contact is the question the GRAMA records were meant to answer.
One witness, two accounts: chest first, then neck. The page tracks when the account changed, and what else changed around it.
Witness after witness described a chest wound rather than a neck wound — the same wrong detail, from people who did not know each other. That repetition is either mass error or a clue.
Dozens of phones were recording. Their combined coverage is more complete than the institutional cameras that were never released, which is why the crowd's footage keeps mattering.
The Israeli forensics firm whose tooling extracted the phones at the centre of the case. Who built the extraction is not a neutral detail when foreign leads are part of the argument.
Lance Twiggs' phone was extracted and entered the record in a case where she is not a defendant. What was taken, and under what authority, is the open question.
Gag orders and sealing keep most of this case out of public view. The page catalogues what has been closed off and on what stated grounds.
Detained, named, released. The page follows what happens to a young man the FBI publicly attaches to a case for a few hours and then lets go.
Who from TPUSA was where at 12:23, and what each of them said afterwards. The staff timeline is where the post-shot minutes get reconstructed.

A Daily Wire editor pulled into this case by one anonymous post about the interior of a room, and by nothing else. He answered with timestamped footage. The page keeps the allegation and the denial side by side without adjudicating either.

The ATF DNA section chief the defense called, who reportedly gave the rifle statistic its ceiling and then explained under cross what a likelihood ratio cannot tell you. Transfer scenarios and error rates went on the record the same afternoon.

The UVU chapter president who helped bring Charlie Kirk to campus. His value to the investigation is upstream of the courtyard: who approved the visit, what security was asked for, and what the answer was.

She reportedly put the Hamptons meeting to Seth Dillon under oath, and commentary says his account shifted afterwards. Asking a question in a proceeding is an ordinary act; what it reportedly produced is why this page exists.
A Deputy Utah County Attorney on the prosecution team, documented by docket entry and public role only. Watch the office rather than the man: discovery disputes and gag-order fights run through it.
A page that exists to close a rumour rather than carry it. Charlie Kirk was married to Erika Kirk, and the fringe framing is recorded only so that no unnamed person gets tarred by it.

The UVU officer reported to have reached the Losee Center roof first, and the State's first live witness at the preliminary hearing. What his body camera did and did not capture became a question of its own.

A Peak Prosperity analyst whose ballistics breakdown argues the wounding pattern fits a fragmenting high-velocity 9mm rather than the .30-06 of the official account. His stated opinion, attributed to him, and one reason the weapon question stays open.

A Deputy Utah County Attorney found in civil contempt in June 2026 over pretrial media statements about "ample evidence" — reportedly made while an ATF ballistics result was inconclusive. The finding concerns publicity rules, not guilt.

The RNC Youth Advisory Council chair photographed among reported participants at the August 2025 Bridgehampton gathering. Placement in a photograph is the whole of the claim; what was said in that room remains unconfirmed.
Named in compiled accounts as one of the EMS crew who arrived in full gear and reportedly asked to be let through. The same accounts say the medics were turned away.

A name inside a chain-of-coincidence thread: a BYU overlap, and a reported summer scribe job at the hospital Charlie Kirk was taken to. The thread's own authors call it coincidence, and this page keeps it labelled that way.

The FBI's Deputy Director, listed at the September 11 briefing and named repeatedly in citizen appeals asking the bureau to ground a private aircraft for forensic review. The appeals are the story here, not any allegation against him.
Credited in commentary with the claim that EMS were "nowhere to be found" at UVU — a characterisation the same compiled notes say video contradicts. A disputed remark, recorded as disputed.

The contractor who says on camera that he was called to lay pavers over the UVU courtyard on September 14, four days after the shooting. Contracted landscaping is lawful work; the question the clip raises is who ordered it, and why then.
